asA: beta reader relying on the referee-guarantees page to know what `rcf define validate` proves
iWant: a broken ADR supersededBy or relatedAdrs pointer to be reported as a brokenReference the same way a broken parent link is
soThat: the docs-page promise that every reference in every document resolves is enforced by the tool, not by convention
title: US-16001: define validate walks ADR supersededBy and relatedAdrs

acceptanceCriteria.description: An ADR whose supersededBy names an id with no file on disk (or an id that resolves to a non-ADR kind) surfaces as a brokenReference error naming the ADR file and the field `supersededBy`, and the corresponding target id joins tree.brokenIds. A supersededBy field that is absent or empty is silent.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an initialised RCF project with adr-001.json whose supersededBy is set to a non-existent id ADR-999
acceptanceCriteria.when: walkTree runs (as invoked by `rcf define validate`)
acceptanceCriteria.then: errors contain a brokenReference with documentId ADR-001 and field supersededBy naming ADR-999, and tree.brokenIds contains ADR-999

acceptanceCriteria.description: An ADR whose relatedAdrs contains an id with no file on disk surfaces as a brokenReference error naming the ADR file and the array index (relatedAdrs[i]). Every unknown entry is surfaced (per-index, not a single collapsed error). An empty or absent relatedAdrs is silent.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an initialised RCF project with adr-001.json whose relatedAdrs is set to [ADR-777]
acceptanceCriteria.when: walkTree runs (as invoked by `rcf define validate`)
acceptanceCriteria.then: errors contain a brokenReference with documentId ADR-001 whose field starts with relatedAdrs, and tree.brokenIds contains ADR-777
